To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
ICAM-1 is expressed by endothelium and stromal cells of human endometrium across the menstrual cycle.
ICAM- 1 expression in the endothelium is not altered by either the hormonal or inflammatory milieu of the endometrium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the expression of ICAM in the human endometrium.
the expression of intercellular adhesions in the human endometrium, and how these molecules are altered by hormonal contraception and the menstrual cycle.
the role of ICAM- 1 in neutrophil infiltration into the endometrium during the pre-menstrual phase and in long-term progestogen only contraception (LTPCC).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

ICAM- 1 expression in the endometrium does not appear to change across the menstrual cycle or with LTPOC treatment and that the neutrophil infiltration in the premenstrum and with LTPOC may not be related to altered expression of endothelial cell ICAM-1.
ICAM- 1 is expressed on endometrial endothelial cells but not on endometrial stromal cells or glands, and that its expression does not change across the menstrual cycle or during LTPOC treatment.
the ICAM-1 immunostaining pattern is not altered across the menstrual cycle in endometrial biopsys, nor in those of women using LTPOC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
ICAM- 1 expression is not altered in LTPOC derived endometrium and is not a cause of neutrophil influx.
the endometrium has an inflammatory response to the progestin-only contraceptive.
the ICAM-1 immunostaining pattern in the endothelium is consistent across the menstrual cycle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression of ICAM1 in the endometrium is limited to endothelial cells, and that ICAM1 expression does not appear to vary in a cyclical fashion.
ICAM- 1 is expressed in the endometrium by both endothelial and stromal cells, but the intensity of expression varies between these two types of cell.
there are no changes in ICAM-1 in the endometrium during the menstrual cycle.
